title: Mean exposure does not provide the required concentration
statement: Deterministic pathwise per-label cumulative adverse budgets earn a backward-product transform even with instantaneous bursts, actual bounded batch participation and adapted history. Priced exhaustion uses ghosts initialized at ACTUAL current rank, preserves genuine allocation and pays probability of too many exhausted labels; future realized exposure is never inserted into the test. Continuous compensator assumption excludes unpriced adverse atoms. Uniform UNCONDITIONAL exponential exposure moments of order eta>1 yield stated polynomial target-count and polynomial exceptional-probability consequence after B=gamma log n,T=n^-delta, with admissible constants C<eta and L eta delta<eta-C. Order-one adversarial construction has bounded moment1+pB yet target chance <=qT exp(-1/T)+qexp(-2/T), defeating uniform polynomial count. It is horizon-dependent finite-rate retained-history control, not a fixed raw law or a counterexample to restartable conditional certificates. Raw exposure acquisition, stopped Green, births/deletions and global recurrence remain separate.

Each theorem retains its own fixed-population or admissible immigration/pure-deletion seed contract, actual first-terminal stopping and output loss, frozen ordinary labels, exact trace clock and reward-weighted potential.

Uniform/null-slot reset and without-replacement sampling laws for exact carried profiles; a matching mean alone is insufficient. Abstract control converses require free nonnegative finite-rate intensities with no common upper bound.
